target_customer: Developers and small teams who want an analytical database without running ClickHouse themselves
problem: Operating an analytical database means handling server configuration, ingestion, queries, replication and sharding. ScratchDB wrapped ClickHouse behind simple insert and query endpoints.
business_model: Open source core (AGPL-3.0) with a paid hosted version

founders.name: Len Boyette
prior_employers: Okta (early engineer, founded developer experience team)
founders.background_notes: Solo founder per the YC page; maintained open source projects with over a billion installs.

technical_complexity.rationale: Built on ClickHouse, so the hard engine work was borrowed; the difficulty was operating, scaling and abstracting it for a one person team.

defensibility.rationale: The core was open source under AGPL and sat on another open source engine, so copying was easy for well funded managed ClickHouse vendors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying event found. The 2023 Show HN thread compared it to Tinybird and GraphJSON.

market_need_then: Demand for fast analytics on large event volumes was established, but no evidence of customer pull for ScratchDB itself was found.

branding.community_and_virality: A Show HN post in October 2023 and about 2.2K GitHub stars per StackShare

brand_strength.rationale: Some developer attention from Show HN and GitHub, but the name collides with the MIT Scratch language and with an unrelated Scratch stats project, so search and recall were weak.

outcome_analysis: Scratch Data was a one person YC Summer 2021 company that sold a managed ClickHouse database and open sourced the core in 2023. YC lists it as inactive but no announcement, closure date or cause is public. The product showed open source traction on GitHub, yet no revenue or customer data was found, so the cause stays unknown and no failure factors are assigned.
notes: Site scratchdata.com did not resolve from the research environment. Funding: CB Insights shows a 500K convertible note dated 1 Jan 2021 (placeholder date, YC as investor); Dealroom shows a 125K seed. Single database basis, amount unreliable. No dated competitor sources near mid 2021 were found; Tinybird appears only in a 2023 thread, so it is excluded. Exit type unknown because YC status gives no detail.
